whyItMatters: For founders building agentic products, latency directly impacts user experience and cost; SMC offers a practical way to speed up agents without sacrificing quality.

whyItMatters: For founders building AI that parses legal documents, this highlights the risk of relying on single parsers and the need for robust validation against inter-parser disagreement.

whatToTry.note: The paper shows that global error models can fail—so test your validation on specific legal domains or jurisdictions.

items.title: 98% of Claims Adjusters Hate AI: What Founders Must Know

whyItMatters: Business impact: Founders selling AI to insurance or similar industries face significant user resistance; ignoring this can lead to failed deployments and reputational damage.
Technical impact: AI tools must be designed to augment rather than replace human roles, with transparent workflows and clear human oversight to build trust.

whatToTry.description: If you're building AI for insurance or other professional services, conduct user research with frontline workers (e.g., adjusters) to identify their pain points and fears. Design your product to assist, not automate, their decisions—emphasize human-in-the-loop features and provide training that positions AI as a tool to reduce mundane tasks, not as a replacement.
whatToTry.note: Consider piloting with a small group of skeptical users to gather feedback and iterate on trust-building features.
